subject: Re: PayMate incident — log access scope for exec briefing
messages:
From: Alan White <alan.white@paymate.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: PayMate outage — request for incident-time logs and scope

Vanessa —

Thanks for taking the call earlier. PayMate's execs are asking for a compact, auditable package we can use in our internal postmortem and for a short board update. Specifically we need:

- A time-bounded set of logs for 2027-04-01 18:00:00 UTC through 2027-04-01 20:30:00 UTC focused on the production inference cluster that served our traffic.
- Per-route latency histograms and error-rate samples (500ms+ buckets, 5xx types).
- A timestamped access history for those artifacts (who pulled, what roles).
- Confirmation there was no exposure of customer API keys or raw prompt text; if any prompt-level logs must be redacted, please describe how.
- Preferred format: signed archive (SHA256) and a short manifest describing redactions.

Can your team confirm what you can provide today vs what needs legal/exec sign-off? Alan (cc ops).

—Alan
Alan White
VP Ops — PayMate
alan.white@paymate.com


From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alan White <alan.white@paymate.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PayMate outage — request for incident-time logs and scope

Alan —

Thanks — we hear the urgency. Looping in Marissa (Customer Success) and Sean (Runtime Ops) to scope the artifacts and Evelyn (Legal) to confirm any required coverings. High-level plan from our side:

1) We can prepare a limited forensic bundle (logs + metrics) scoped to the timestamps you specified.
2) We will produce a manifest and perform minimal redaction to remove any plaintext keys or identifiers.
3) For chain-of-custody and signatures we will provide SHA256 checksums and a signed cover letter; if you need a notarized affidavit, that will need a short legal process.

Marissa / Sean: can you confirm what exact artifacts we can stage by EOD PST and which need additional approvals? Evelyn: please advise what format/payments/legal cover we need before sharing artifacts externally.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, alan.white@paymate.com
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PayMate outage — request for incident-time logs and scope

Thanks Vanessa / Alan —

Operationally, here's the minimal set we can assemble quickly (ETA EOD PST):
- per-route latency histogram (aggregated CSV) for the 2.5 hour window (attachment: paymate_latency_histogram.csv)
- sampled request events (anonymized): 1,000 rows with timestamp, route, status_code, duration_ms, latency_bucket
- sampled 5xx error stack snippets (redacted) — limited to 50 events
- runtime telemetry (span IDs + durations) and a mapping to our internal job ids (will be in the manifest)
- access log lines for S3/object retrievals for the artifacts we upload (start/end times + principal id)

Redaction notes: we will replace any prompt text and any API keys with <REDACTED>. We do not persist customer API keys or secrets in plain text in production logs; any trace of tokens would be masked at collection time, but we'll confirm via a scoped grep.

Attachments: forensic_artifacts_manifest.txt (draft) shows fields and redaction approach. If PayMate legal needs a narrower subset (e.g., no sampled prompts at all) tell us and we'll remove them.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Alan White <alan.white@paymate.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@legalpay.co>, ops@paymate.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PayMate outage — request for incident-time logs and scope

Marissa — appreciate the quick breakdown. Two clarifications from our side:

1) For the exec briefing we need a verifiable chain-of-custody: who exported what and when (ideally IAM principal + timestamp + IP if available).
2) Can you confirm that there were no plaintext customer API keys in the sample exports? If you detect any, we need immediate notification and a description of the exposure window.

Also, we'll need a short accompanying statement (1 paragraph) that a Redwood exec can sign confirming the artifact integrity for our board. If you need our legal to sign an NDA or cover letter, Jordan (cc) will coordinate.

Alan

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, alan.white@paymate.com
Cc: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PayMate outage — request for incident-time logs and scope

Alan / team —

Quick technical details on what we can provide and constraints:

- Storage: forensic snapshots will be exported from our ephemeral forensic bucket (S3) that is KMS-encrypted. Keys are customer-isolated for Dedicated/private customers; for hosted customers we rotate EKs every 24h. We will include the KMS key-id used for encryption in the manifest.
- Access history: we can provide object-level access logs (principal + action + timestamp). Our internal ops access is via SSO (Okta) and service principals; I can map principal ids to human names in the manifest.
- Redaction: prompt-level fields will be redacted server-side before export. We'll replace with consistent tokens (<PROMPT_REDACTED_n>) so PayMate can reference samples without exposing text.
- Integrity: we'll produce a tar.gz and an accompanying SHA256 file; Sean Gallagher will sign the manifest with the company PGP key.
- API keys: we do not log live API secrets. Any token traces are truncated in logs — I'll run a grep to confirm none made it into the samples.

I will prepare the bundle and place it in a presigned S3 URL with 72-hour expiry. Legal sign-off needed for distribution to PayMate execs — Evelyn, can you confirm the wording we use in the cover letter?

-Sean
Senior Runtime Engineer — Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: alan.white@paymate.com, jordan.lee@legalpay.co
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PayMate outage — request for incident-time logs and scope

Team / Alan —

Legal is OK to proceed with a limited-distribution forensic package under the following conditions: 

1) Minimal dataset only (aggregates + sampled, redacted rows) — no raw prompt dumps.
2) Signed manifest and SHA256 checksums attached to the package.
3) Access will be via a presigned S3 link with a 72-hour TTL; logging of S3 GETs will be included in the manifest.
4) We will require PayMate to sign a short data handling addendum (DocuSign link) before we hand off the full bundle to their execs; Jordan, please coordinate.

Action items for Redwood Ops/CS: create internal evidence ticket (INF-9321), upload the artifact bundle to the support-forensics S3 bucket, generate SHA256 + PGP signature, and attach redaction_checklist.pdf to the package. Vanessa: please confirm the exec who needs the signed cover letter so we can prepare it.

Evelyn Hart
Legal Counsel — Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
